_meta.purpose: The exact check contexts that main's ruleset requires, and the workflow trigger conditions that make each one reportable on every pull request. Prepared by M29-A.
_meta.context_names_are_job_names: A required status check context is the *job* name, not the workflow name. These strings must match byte for byte.
_meta.middle_dot_warning: Five of the seven contexts contain U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT (·), not a hyphen and not a full stop. Copy them; do not retype them. A mistyped context never reports, and a required check that never reports leaves every pull request pending forever — the same end state as a broken gate, reached by a different route.
_meta.the_path_filter_trap: GitHub treats a required check that does not report as PENDING, never as satisfied. Before M29-A, four of the five workflows below filtered their `pull_request` trigger by path, so a documentation-only pull request would have hung indefinitely waiting for checks that were never going to run. M29-A removes `paths:` from `pull_request` in those workflows while keeping it on `push`, so every check reports a conclusion on every pull request and post-merge runs stay narrow.

actionlint over every file in .github/workflows — YAML syntax, Actions semantics, expression contexts, and shellcheck over run: blocks — plus a five-case negative control that proves the gate rejects what it should and accepts what it should.
required.note: Added by M29-I. The workflow's pull_request paths filter was removed first: GitHub treats a required check that never reports as pending rather than satisfied, so requiring a path-filtered check would leave every pull request that touches no workflow permanently unmergeable. The job name was aligned to this context in the same change, because GitHub matches on the job name and not the workflow name. This check exists because release.yml was unloadable for two weeks and nothing was asking whether the gates could run at all.

required.covers: A fail-closed aggregator over the two Flutter certification jobs. Green only when BOTH `Android · doctor · analyze · test · build apk` and `iOS · analyze · test · build (no codesign)` report success — analyze under --fatal-infos --fatal-warnings, the full test suite, a release APK with if-no-files-found: error, and an iOS no-codesign build.
required.note: Added by M33. The context is the AGGREGATOR job name, deliberately, and the two platform jobs are NOT individually required: requiring them would pin two more byte-exact strings containing U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT into the ruleset, so any later rename would stop them reporting and block every pull request. The aggregator runs with `if: always()` because bare `needs:` SKIPS a dependent job when a dependency fails, and GitHub treats a skipped required check as pending rather than failed — the same trap this file documents from M29-A. `always()` alone would be the opposite defect, so the job compares needs.android.result and needs.ios.result against the literal 'success' and fails on anything else, including cancelled, skipped and any result GitHub adds later. Do not confuse this with `Analyse · Test`, which is the job name inside ci-mobile.yml (workflow `CI · Mobile (Flutter)`) and is a different check that remains deliberately not required.

deliberately_not_required.reason: Fails on main today and failed identically at cbdc2ab, 8a2a2e8, 4615bdc, beb5c09 and fc412dc. Requiring a check that is already red would block every pull request on a pre-existing condition M29-A did not introduce and does not fix.
deliberately_not_required.follow_up: Diagnose separately. It should become required once it is green, and its current state is itself worth an investigation.

deliberately_not_required.reason: Tag-triggered only (`push: tags: ["v*.*.*"]`). It produces a zero-job startup-failure entry on every branch push and has done so on every merge to main since at least beb5c09. It cannot report on a pull request, so requiring it would leave every pull request pending forever.
Not part of the M28 evidence set and not analysed by M29-A. Left out rather than required on an assumption.
deliberately_not_required.follow_up: Audit its trigger conditions and job name before considering it.

deliberately_not_required.reason: Added by M37 Phase 4B. It reports what GitHub is actually enforcing, which is exactly the question no other check asks — but two of its findings are accepted governance gaps recorded in .github/governance/known-gaps.json, and one of them (the absent production tag ruleset) can only be closed by an administrative change to live GitHub state. Requiring the context while a known-and-accepted gap is open would block every pull request on a condition no pull request can fix.
deliberately_not_required.advisory_does_not_mean_it_cannot_fail: The job carries no continue-on-error, no `|| true` and no forced exit 0. A new governance failure, a recorded gap that has silently resolved, or evidence that could not be fetched all turn it red. It blocks nothing because it is absent from the ruleset — not because it was built unable to fail. .github/scripts/governance_advisory_wiring.py enforces that distinction from inside the required `CI · Workflow Integrity` context.
deliberately_not_required.follow_up: Consider requiring it once .github/governance/known-gaps.json is empty. The job name is already the permanent context string, so promotion needs no rename — M29-I's finding is that renaming a job detaches any rule requiring the old name.

verification.after_applying: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets/{id} and compare rules[].parameters.required_status_checks[].context against `required[].context` above, exactly.
verification.what_local_cannot_prove: That GitHub is enforcing any of it. The validator checks that the contexts exist as job names and that the workflows will report on pull requests; whether the ruleset is active is an EXTERNAL / ADMIN REQUIRED item and is never reported as PASS.
